subject.title: Windows: lstat bottleneck causes 2-3x slower performance vs Mac (59% of CPU time)

question: Should OpenClaw accept operation-scoped realpath caches in plugin hook/skill discovery and sandbox host-path containment as the fix for this Windows lstat bottleneck?
rationale: The performance problem is concrete, but the remaining fix path changes cache lifetime around containment-sensitive checks, which needs maintainer security-boundary intent before the issue can be resolved.

options.title: Accept scoped caches after PR repair
options.body: Fix and reprove the linked PR, then land operation-scoped caches with tests showing stale symlink/junction changes are not reused across operations.

options.title: Limit caching to non-containment metadata
options.body: Keep the merged manifest-registry cache and reject hook/skill/sandbox containment caches if maintainers decide any reuse there is too risky.

options.title: Request a narrower replacement PR
options.body: Close or pause the stale candidate PR and ask for a smaller replacement that preserves the same cache lifetime contract with fresh Windows proof.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped caches after PR repair
recommendation.body: Fix and reprove the linked PR, then land operation-scoped caches with tests showing stale symlink/junction changes are not reused across operations.
